0.long_answer: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) is most commonly due to a deficiency in the enzymes involved in cortisol synthesis, which takes place in the adrenal cortex. Cortisol is primarily synthesized in the zona fasciculata, a region of the adrenal cortex. In CAH, particularly with 21-hydroxylase deficiency, the impaired enzyme activity in the adrenal cortex reduces cortisol production and leads to compensatory overproduction of ACTH. This results in adrenal hyperplasia and a buildup of upstream steroid precursors, further highlighting the central role of the adrenal cortex in the pathophysiology of CAH.
